q: What is the benefit of specifying concrete with 40% fly ash replacing Portland cement under LEED V5?

It improves fire resistance; Energy & Atmosphere credit
It reduces concrete water use during mixing; Water Efficiency credit
It improves concrete compressive strength; Innovation credit

keywords: Match the term, scope, or function in the question to the exact LEED concept; decisive answer: It significantly reduces the concrete's embodied carbon.
logic: Portland cement production releases approximately 0.9 kg CO₂ per kg through limestone calcination. Replacing 40% with fly ash (a power plant byproduct) can reduce concrete GWP by 30–40%. An EPD documents the verified reduction, supporting LEED's whole-building LCA and building product disclosure credits.

evidence_en: Portland cement production releases approximately 0.9 kg CO₂ per kg through limestone calcination. Replacing 40% with fly ash (a power plant byproduct) can reduce concrete GWP by 30–40%. An EPD documents the verified reduction, supporting LEED's whole-building LCA and building product disclosure credits.

keywords: Choose the option that addresses the stated LEED intent most directly, not a secondary benefit; decisive option: Selecting low-GWP, zero-ODP refrigerants and preventing leaks.
logic: LEED's refrigerant management credits require avoiding high-ODP refrigerants and minimizing GWP by selecting low-GWP alternatives (R-32, R-1234yf) and preventing leaks through proper equipment maintenance.
